releases.name: Anka 1.0.1
releases.body:
**Anka 1.0.1** opens games stored as **.nup** packages.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `2d17a71ff0f0cf0c27b3d7207818fade9199b77b`; both programs carry this commit.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Close Anka, unzip **`Anka-1.0.1-win64.zip`** into your Anka folder and replace the files. Your `user` folder (settings, keys, firmware and saves) stays as it is.

New to Anka: follow the quick start in the [1.0.0 notes](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/releases/tag/anka-v1.0.0). Unzip into a new, empty folder, start `anka.exe`, and install your own keys and firmware.

## What's in 1.0.1

### .nup packages
- `.nup` ("Unencrypted (Archival) Package") is a container format from upstream Eglantine. It holds one title's base game, update and add-on content in a single file.
- Anka now **reads** .nup files. You can open them with **File › Load File…**, and they appear in the game list with their icon, name and version. `anka-cli.exe` and its launchers open them too, including from the `Games` folder.
- Mods (LayeredFS) and Anka's game-specific settings apply to games opened from a .nup, the same as for other formats. Anka finds the title ID before the game starts.

releases.name: Anka 1.0.0
releases.body:
First release of **Anka**, a Nintendo Switch 2 emulator for Windows, focused on performance.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `b7542ece8b5c695e2f01d5e46b74c0806d48ae96`; both programs carry this commit.

## Quick start

1. Unzip **`Anka-1.0.0-win64.zip`** into a **new, empty folder**. Do not unzip it into another emulator's folder: its Qt DLLs would replace that program's.
2. Start **`anka.exe`**. Anka keeps its settings, keys, firmware and saves in the `user` folder next to it (portable mode) and does not touch `%APPDATA%\eden` or other installs.
3. Install your own keys and firmware as with other Eden-based emulators. Anka includes no games, keys or firmware; only use what you legally own.
4. Settings: **Emulation › Configure… › Anka**. The first start picks *Recommended*, the setup we measured (with GPU Mode *Fast*, the default; it also turns Reactive Flushing off).

Coming from PokeDinner-Eglantine 2.0.0: back up its `nand` folder (your saves), then copy its `user` folder next to `anka.exe`.

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a current Vulkan driver. Qt and the Visual C++ runtime come with Anka.

Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64.AppImage, for 4K, 16K and 64K page kernels alike
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

releases.name: FF7Recomp 1.1.62
releases.body:
**Fixed: crashes in some scenes with Echo-S voices and ChaOS's Resized Models (#91)**

Reported in issue #91: with Echo-S 7's voices on, the game closed in some scenes, for example on boarding the Highwind from the world map.

Two mods were each changing half of the same scene. ChaOS's **BETA: Resized Models** option replaces the list of character models for 693 scenes, a list made to match the original game's scene scripts. Echo-S's voiced version brings its own scene scripts, and in 39 scenes those use more characters than ChaOS's list loads. In the Highwind's deck, for example, the scripts use 14 models and ChaOS's list has 10. The game then tried to animate a character that was never loaded and crashed on the first frame. (ChaOS's own description of the option warns that it can crash with gameplay mods.)

Now, when a mod's model list doesn't match the models the scene's scripts use, that list is left out for that scene, and the scene keeps the models that came with its own file. In those 39 scenes the characters have their normal size instead of ChaOS's resized one; everywhere else Resized Models works as before. The log (`ff7.log`) names each scene where this happens.

releases.name: v1.1.61
releases.body:
**Fixed: rare crashes at scene changes with sound-effect mods on (#90)**

Reported in issue #90: once in a while the game closed when entering a battle, leaving the menu, or moving between areas, more often with many mods on and little free memory. The crash records all showed the same thing: some other part of the app had a pointer whose lower half had been overwritten with zeros earlier on.

We tracked it down with a special memory-checking build on our test device, which caught it within a minute. The cause was in FFNx's sound-effect code, which is active whenever a mod replaces the game's sound effects (Echo-S, the Tsunamods set and others). It keeps one record per sound channel. Some calls used the wrong channel number, and every battle transition touched a channel that had no record. Each time, the game wrote a few bytes just past the end of that table, usually zeros, into memory that belonged to something else. Most of the time nothing happened; sometimes it hit a pointer, and whatever used that pointer next crashed.

releases.name: v1.1.60
releases.body:
**Fixed: the game could close a while after loading a save state from an earlier session (#91)**

Reported in issue #91 with Echo-S 7 voices on. The game keeps one data file open the whole time it runs: the sound archive it loads its own sound effects from. A save state stores the game's memory, and that memory held the open file's handle as it was in the session where the state was made. After you closed the game and loaded the state in a later session, that handle no longer pointed at anything. The next time a scene needed a sound the game hadn't loaded yet, the game crashed.

Whether you hit this depended on luck. It was more likely with mods that open many files, like Echo-S voices.

Save states now record which files the game has open, and opening them again is part of loading a state. States made with older versions are covered too: the sound archive is opened again when they load.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. It asks to **Update the game** once (a few seconds).

APK SHA-256: `f29167fd9f2e8d88814386aacf28742669a42cc58810be4dca13f5972d3dd3ab`

releases.name: v1.1.59
releases.body:
**New: the launcher says what kind of device runs the game best, and what helps after a crash**

Suggested in issue #90. Rare crashes when a battle or scene is drawn for the first time are most often the phone running low on memory while the graphics driver prepares that scene's shaders. That is a hardware limit more than a bug, so the launcher now says so where you'll see it:

- **After the game crashes** (or Android closes it for memory), the launcher shows a short note once: what most often causes it, what helps, and a button to **Report a problem** if it keeps happening.
- **Report a problem** and **Game files** (first setup) show the recommendation.
- **Settings → Renderer** now recommends **OpenGL ES** on Mali GPUs (most MediaTek and Exynos phones).
- The README has the same line under *Playing*.

The recommendation: **8 GB of RAM or more, with other apps (browser tabs too) closed while you play.** Heavy mod sets need the most memory, above all on Vulkan. On Mali GPUs, OpenGL ES is usually the steadier choice.

![The note the launcher shows once after the game crashed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/main/docs/release-images/1.1.59-crash-tip.jpg)

releases.name: v1.1.58
releases.body:
**Fixed: the graphics-driver crash protection from 1.1.57 now covers OpenGL ES too**

1.1.57 started keeping the game's finished GPU programs on your device when you play on Vulkan, so the graphics driver doesn't have to compile them again on every launch (that compiler is where the crash in issue #90 happened). Many players use OpenGL ES instead, because Vulkan is slower on their phone, so the same now happens there: once the game has drawn something on OpenGL ES, later launches load the finished program instead of compiling it again.

If your driver ever refuses one of the kept programs (for example after a driver update), the game simply builds it again the normal way. As before, the first time you reach a scene still has to compile it, so this makes the crash less likely rather than impossible.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. It asks to **Update the game** once (a few seconds).

The first release since [0.3.0](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.3.0): a faster game, a picture closer to the console's, and two experimental options that make it faster still.

## New

- **Faster on every level.** The emulated kernel woke every waiting thread whenever anything was signalled (one of the game's locks is released some 50,000 times a second); now only the threads waiting for that object wake. The game's CPU use dropped from about 5.4 cores to 3.3, and the forest at 1080p without MSAA went from about 91 to 95–108 frames a second.
- **Native command lists (experimental)**, in the F11 menu, after a restart. The draws are made from the game's own Direct3D calls, and the console's GPU command stream is run only for what the GPU still has to do. With **Watch memory writes (experimental)** also on, the forest at 1080p without MSAA runs at about 180 frames a second. Tested on eight levels, the films and mission restarts; off by default until it has been played more.

releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.2](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.2), and the one worth updating for: the lighting is right now.

## Fixed

**Walls lit far too brightly, and the odd shading on the soldiers and on the player's hands.** An instruction of the console's shaders has a vector half and a scalar half, and they run together: both read the registers as they were before the instruction and only then write. The translation wrote the vector's result first, so a scalar that read the very register the vector wrote got the new value instead of the old one.

The game's third light per surface is written exactly that way. Its scalar wants the specular exponent times a logarithm; with the write first it took a dot product instead, and two to the tenth of that became the specular. Every lit stone wall in Mayenne came out white with pink and green speckle, and characters were shaded oddly for the same reason. Eighty of the six hundred shader programs a level draws with have such an instruction, so this shows up all over the game, not only on that wall.

## Known issues

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.2.2
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.1](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.1); everything below is on top of what 0.2.1 brought.

## Fixed

**The HUD and the menu still flickered.** 0.2.1 looked at every texture every frame again, but a large one that had been still for a while was only *sampled*: sixty four places out of it. The HUD's fonts, icons and compass are small and change a handful of texels at a time, and the samples missed those changes, so the old picture stayed up for a frame. Everything up to two megabytes is now hashed whole, every frame, and only what is bigger than that falls back to sampling.

**Shadow filtering collapsed.** A texture fetch on the console carries three signed offsets in halves of a texel. The game's shadows are one map fetched four times at the corners of a texel; with the offsets dropped those were four fetches of the same texel, so a surface came out wholly lit or wholly dark instead of softly edged.

new update fellas:D this one brings more optimization and bug fixes

This ran pretty well for me but might be troublesome for older phones, so use Fast quality for it to run a bit better.

Frame generation also has a quality setting. High gives Mario, enemies and other moving objects their own motion. Fast follows only the camera and is meant for slower GPUs

## O que mudou nesta branch (`fix/first-launch-crash`)

### Corrigido o crash na 1ª inicialização (selecionar ROM + Start Game fechava o app)
Na primeira execução do app, depois de selecionar a ROM e tocar em **Start Game**, o app fechava sozinho; na segunda inicialização funcionava perfeitamente. Causa raiz multi-fator, todas eliminadas:

## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.body:
Restores compatibility with third-party native mods. If mods failed to load, or loaded and then force-closed the game, this is the fix.

### Fixed

* **Mods failed to load with "Unknown mod load failure".** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  Adding the companion's slot I/II buttons pushed `BTN_R` to `1 << 8` and widened `daAlink_c::itemTriggerCheck` / `itemButtonCheck` from `u8` to `u16`. That changes the mangled names, so mods built against upstream Dusklight could not resolve them and failed at `dlopen`. The upstream symbols are re-exported as forwarders that translate the button numbering as well as the width — upstream's `BTN_B` is `BTN_S2` here, so widening alone would have routed a sword check to a slot button.

  Measured against three mods: only 2 of 842, 762 and 55 game-symbol imports were unresolved.

* **The game force-closed when a loaded mod ran.**

releases.body:
Patch release for **Dual-Screen 3.0**. No gameplay or dual-screen changes — the native code is identical to 3.0.

### Fixed

* **Cosmetics, Luau Support and Randomizer were missing from the Android build.** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  The Android CMake presets listed only the `dusklight` target, so the `dusklight_mods` aggregate target never ran and `bundled_mods/` was never produced. Gradle packs that directory into `assets/mods`, so the APK shipped with no bundled mod packages at all. Mods that depend on the Luau runtime could not load either.

  All three packages are now present: `cosmetics`, `luau_runtime` and `randomizer`.

  CI was never affected — `build.yml` builds `dusklight_mods` as its own explicit `--target` step. This only broke preset-driven local builds.

- Native Metal renderer, EXPERIMENTAL and off by default. Turn it on in Settings > Runtime >
  "Native Metal renderer (Experimental)". It applies from the next game launch. MoltenVK stays
  the default renderer. Metal has been tested on Bloodborne only. Some games may render wrongly or not start with Metal; switch it off if so.

## Performance
- MoltenVK queue submits are asynchronous on iOS: the emulator no longer waits on each submit.
- Metal shader compile workers run at utility QoS, so they compete less with the game threads.

## Fixes (Metal renderer)
- Write protection of pages a pending GPU write targets is held back; the GPU is waited for before wrapped guest pages are unmapped (God of War III boot fault).
- The copy-shader HLE drops elements past the destination buffer.
- Small read-only guest data is copied when a draw binds it.
- A buffer write skips the write-back of images it covers.
- A wait that a pending fence ends submits the queued GPU work.

# Lichii-Enhanced v1.0.0: first public release

Lichii-Enhanced is a fork of [Lichii](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii) focused on usability: easier setup, built-in upscaling, non-destructive modding and more reliable online play. This is the first public release.

> **Platform:** Windows 10/11 x64 only. Distributed as a `.zip` archive. Other platforms are not available yet.

## Highlights

### 🖼️ Built-in upscalers
Upscaling is now part of the renderer; no external injectors or wrappers are needed.

- New post-process stage at the end of the Vulkan frame (compute shaders), running after game rendering and before swapchain presentation
- Filters: Nearest, Bilinear, Bicubic, FSR 1.0 (EASU + RCAS), SGSR
- Configurable render scale and sharpness (RCAS strength)
- Per-game profiles stored in `config/custom/<title-id>.ini`
- Optional anti-aliasing pass before upscaling

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **Desempenho na Grande Ilha do Céu:**
  - Os vértices da ilha ficavam fora da área que a GPU lê direto, e a CPU copiava ~2,5 GB a cada 2 s. Agora são ~250 MB, e o trabalho de vértices da thread de render caiu de ~250 para ~75 ms a cada 2 s (POCO F7 Ultra, Turnip).

releases.body:
**Beta 0.3.4.** Acaba a **queda de fps depois de fechar o inventário** ([#53](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/53), [#24](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/24)) e melhora a **geração de quadros (LSFG)**: importar o `Lossless.dll`, funcionar em mais GPUs Mali e pedir à tela a taxa de atualização que os quadros gerados precisam.

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **Queda depois do menu ([#53](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/53), [#24](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid/issues/24)):**
  - A queda de 12-14 s depois de fechar o inventário, de escolher uma arma ou de salvar não era o clock da GPU, como eu tinha dito.
  - O app desligava o "sync lag" por ~10 s sempre que o jogo saía do mundo, para proteger os carregamentos. Só que ele não distinguia um menu de uma tela de carregamento, e nesses segundos a CPU ficava esperando a GPU.

releases.name: TOTKDroid 0.3.3 (beta): FSR 1 e FXAA mais leves
releases.body:
**Beta 0.3.3.** O **FSR 1** e o **FXAA** ficaram mais leves para a GPU, com a mesma imagem.

> **Nenhum arquivo do jogo vem junto.** Você precisa do seu próprio dump de *Tears of the Kingdom* com a atualização **1.4.3** aplicada (`exefs` e `romfs`, ou o `romfs` como um único `romfs.bin`).

Atualiza por cima das versões anteriores sem apagar os saves. **Não desinstale o app antes**: isso apaga os saves.

## O que mudou

- **FSR 1 (EASU) na metade do tempo:**
  - A análise de borda roda uma vez por pixel, em vez de quatro.
  - Onde não há borda, o pixel sai direto da interpolação bilinear.
  - As contas de cor usam meia precisão, que vira fp16 onde o driver aceita.
  - No POCO F7 Ultra (Adreno 830), o upscale de 1280x717 para 1920x1080 caiu de 1,00 para 0,50 ms por quadro. Não vi diferença nas bordas lado a lado.
  - Ideias do artigo "Optimizing FSR", de atyuwen, reescritas a partir do FSR 1 original.
- **FXAA ~18% mais leve:**
  - Usa meia precisão e o limiar padrão do FXAA 3.11, em vez do "ultra".
  - A busca da borda é mais curta: 5 passos em vez de 10.
  - No POCO caiu de 0,51-0,59 para 0,43-0,44 ms por quadro, sem diferença de serrilhado visível.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.5-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.5-dev (versionCode 9).

### Changes

- Added native implementations of selected game, rendering, AI and container algorithms, with the original recompiled paths retained. Optimized guest-register handling, x87 calculations and indirect-call caches.
- Added Optimal (ARM64) and Exact (x86) execution modes. Exact selects the original recompiled algorithms; both modes run as ARM64 code.
- Reduced GLES state traffic between threads, draw preparation work and shader constant uploads, and improved shader program caching.
- Improved launcher operation progress, diagnostics and Play button feedback, with the amber UT3 palette.
- Added an optional 4 GB guest address space, enabled by default on 64-bit devices with at least 5 GiB of RAM.
- Fixed fingerprint sensors being mistaken for gamepads.
- Reduced APK size by stripping non-runtime library symbols while retaining the original library for offline profiling. Expanded regression tests and updated documentation.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4.1-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4.1-dev (versionCode 8).

### Changes

- Improved CPU performance on PhysX Mod Pack maps with native fluid collision kernels, native pair removal and optimized x87 calculations.
- Added on-device HLSL compilation through vkd3d-shader, with shader caching and improved MojoShader compatibility for mod materials.
- Fixed touch aiming: holding Fire no longer blocks another finger's camera movement; dragging from Fire, secondary fire, Jump or Crouch also turns the camera.
- Made the crash monitor a launcher option, disabled by default, to avoid keeping its extra Android process running unless needed.
- Removed FSR3 frame generation. FSR1 spatial upscaling and FXAA remain available.
- Reduced per-draw post-processing overhead and removed temporary qa-flags performance switches.
- Updated localized PhysX and audio setting descriptions.

### Installation and validation

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; compatible Adreno devices can use Turnip.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4-dev.

### Changes

- Added an FPS counter with a frame-time graph and optional system information for every renderer.
- Added FSR1, FXAA, and FSR3.1 frame generation (DXVK, Android 12+; disabled by default).
- Added CPU-based PhysX effects and OpenAL Soft audio through AAudio with EAX 1–5 support.
- Added a maximum-graphics button and fixed persistence of the 3D rendering scale.
- Fixed terrain rendering in OpenGL ES, accelerated DXT decoding, and allowed unused texture mip levels to stream out.
- Improved GPU query handling in GLES and DXVK, including on PowerVR devices.
- Fixed ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion on shared storage on Pixel devices.
- Added a “Firing or aiming” gyroscope mode and persistent crash reports with a separate error window.

### Installation and limitations

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; frame generation requires Android 12+. Frame generation may cause HUD artifacts and adds GPU and memory overhead. A stable 60 FPS at maximum graphics settings is not guaranteed.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.3-dev
releases.body:
The third release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 improves GLES performance, text editing and graphics cache handling.

### Changes

- Added a dedicated GLES render thread with automatic CPU core selection. Streamed draw uploads, asynchronous query polling and shader program prelinking reduce work on the game thread.
- Added driver-aware graphics cache maintenance: GLES program binaries are invalidated after driver changes, and DXVK keeps the current and newest other pipeline cache for each driver.
- Fixed DXVK scaled vertex formats with a shader fallback for drivers that need it.
- Replaced keyboard-only text entry with an Android editing dialog for game fields, console commands and chat. Existing text can be corrected or cleared; cancellation preserves it, and original character filters remain in effect.
- Added separate weapon-button swipe settings and expanded the in-game Android settings to nine languages: English, Russian, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Polish.
- Improved launcher texture status and fixed texture handling, audio and FSINCOS translation. Expanded regression tests and rendering diagnostics.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 0.2-dev
releases.body:
The second release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 adds optional texture conversion, more flexible touch controls, OpenSpy compatibility and save/profile fixes.

### Changes

- Added optional ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion in the launcher, including games played directly from stored ZIP archives. Original packages are retained; runtime DXT decoding remains available for cache misses and mods.
- Added a touch layout editor to move, resize and hide individual controls. Hold the on-screen Pause button to open it; a short tap opens the original pause menu.
- Expanded touch settings with a fixed joystick, weapon tap/swipe selection, separate weapon bar/wheel sizes, control visibility, movement while holding primary fire and horizontal gyro reversal.
- Added OpenSpy service and authentication compatibility, and fixed a registry-call crash during online play.
- Prevented startup defaults from overwriting saved profiles and campaign progress before sign-in. Fixed creation of save directories beneath virtual ZIP folders.

- Expanded the bounded host-visible buffer cache from 8 MiB to 16 MiB while retaining the 64 MiB LRU cap.

releases.name: v0.7.7
releases.body:
v0.7.7 fixes the Android surface orientation: the v0.7.6 build restored the identity-preferred swapchain preTransform that had shipped in v0.7.5, and on devices reporting ROTATE_90 the composer applied that rotation a second time to an already-upright window-space blit. The game UI rendered sideways and the touch overlay and cursor left the visible area, which is why the on-screen cursor and some options panels (e.g. the Display tab) did not appear where expected.

This release returns the swapchain preTransform to the current display transform, so the composer no longer adds an implicit rotation. Framebuffer, touch overlay, and cursor share one orientation again.

- `preTransform` is now `cap.currentTransform` in `nvn_vulkan.c` (the code path that shipped in the working v0.7.4 build), instead of identity-preferred. Log line `[vulkan-surface-transform]` prints the supported / current / selected masks each session; expect `selected` to equal `current`.

releases.body:
# Swap2-Native 0.2.0.2-beta

Less memory trouble in heavy places, a clearer "Compiling shaders" screen, and Pokémon Pokopia's shader update made short.

**Install over 0.2.0.1-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A game that slows to a crawl when the phone runs out of memory** (Zelda: Ocarina of Time entering Castle Town on a 16 GB phone fell to under 1 fps for minutes). The texture cache now notices when the phone starts swapping the game out and stops growing instead. If a game still stutters in big areas, turn on **RAM saving** (Game settings) and close other apps.
- **Zelda: Ocarina of Time on phones with 12 GB of RAM or less** uses less memory for textures and graphics memory (from Banana Native).
- **The "Compiling shaders" screen** shows its whole text on two lines (the time left and "Tap to skip" were cut off), and its bar follows the count.
- **Pokémon Pokopia** updates its shaders quickly after installing 0.2.0: about 60 shaders instead of all of them.

releases.name: Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta
releases.body:
# Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta

A fix for 0.2.0-beta: no more black screen while a game prepares its pipelines.

**Install over 0.2.0-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is translated or prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A black screen at the first start of a game** (seen with Turnip drivers, for example on a Redmagic 11 Air). Since 0.2.0, a game prepares its known pipelines before it plays (at most 90 seconds). The loading screen had already gone by then, so the game looked stuck. Now the loading screen stays and shows **Compiling shaders: N of M**; tap it to skip the rest. On Turnip the pipelines are made one at a time, so the first start takes the full 90 seconds unless you skip; the next starts are short.

Everything else is as in [0.2.0-beta](https://github.com/mamcjr/Swap2-Native/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta).

## Thanks

**moceure and the Banana Native contributors**, **enjoyerofslop / DroidPlay Core**, **Sergii "iOrange" Kudlai** (bcdec), **erickmendes22** and **EddizEge / AnkaNative**. Licenses and attribution are included in the sources.

# Nimbus Alpha 2.2.2 for Android

A second hotfix for Android. Linux and Windows stay on 2.2.1.

## Fixed

- **Phones that still showed "Nimbus could not start graphics" on 2.2.1** (for example some Helio G99 phones on Android 14) now start their games. On these phones Nimbus uses a second graphics path.
- Heads up: the second graphics path is slower than Vulkan, so games on those phones may run slower. Every other device stays on Vulkan.
- Every other device runs exactly as on 2.2.1.

## Good to know

- After updating, Nimbus prepares its shaders once more on the first start.
- Online play is unchanged: 2.2.2 on Android plays with 2.2, 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 on every platform.

## Updating

Install the 2.2.2 APK over 2.2 or 2.2.1. It updates in place and keeps your links and saves. Do not uninstall first.

Thanks to Velkooky on Reddit for finding and reporting this bug.

The first release of Odin.

Odin (ᚨ) is a low-level emulator of the SEGA Hikaru arcade board. It runs the programs of the real chips wherever they are known, and draws with OpenGL or Vulkan. It is a hard fork of Valkyrie, by Stefano Teso.

## Games

All six Hikaru games, two of them in two versions:

- Air Trix (`airtrix`, `airtrixo`)
- Brave Firefighters (`braveff`)
- Planet Harriers (`pharrier`)
- NASCAR Arcade (`sgnascar`, `sgnascaro`)
- Star Wars Racer Arcade (`swracer`)
- Cyber Troopers Virtual-On Force (`von4`)

They play with a keyboard, mice, gamepads, wheels with force feedback (NASCAR) or light guns (Brave Firefighters). Each game is a MAME ROM and needs the BIOS `hikaru.zip` and `mie.zip` too.

### Installing

1. Install `smrpg-recomp-android-0.9.1-alpha.apk` (Android 13 or newer, 64-bit ARM, Vulkan 1.3).
2. Compile the game's code for your device (`lasgame.so`) from your extracted copy, on a Windows PC: [README, "Building"](https://github.com/ElKiro1311/smrpg-recompiled-android#building). The APK contains nothing of the game, so it can't do this step for you yet.

**SMRPG Recomp for Android**: an unofficial port of *Super Mario RPG* (Nintendo Switch, 2023, version 1.0.0) to Android by static recompilation, on top of the [LASRecomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp) runtime. It is an **alpha**.

### What's new

- **The settings menu is in English**, and in Spanish when the game's language is Spanish (Video > Game language). With "Automatic" it follows the system's language.
- The whole repository is in English now: code, log messages, scripts and documents. The README is also [in Spanish](https://github.com/ElKiro1311/smrpg-recompiled-android/blob/main/README.es.md).
- New names, in English, for the HD texture folders (`textures/` and `textures-dump/`) and for the test environment file (`env.txt`). The earlier ones still work.

**Updating from 0.9.1-alpha:** install the APK on top. Your saves, your settings and the game code you already built (`lasgame.so`) stay as they are: there is nothing to build again.
